cases.report_quote: Audience is checked against `RESOURCE`. The check accepts a string or a list of audiences.
cases.reason: The report cites gateway.py:10-22, where authenticate checks RESOURCE against a scalar or list aud. It makes no audience-bypass claim.

cases.report_quote: The key does include the tenant, subject and tool grants, so I found no cross-tenant leak in the key design.
cases.reason: The report treats tenant isolation as likely_pass. The only cache gap it raises is missing invalidation after a delete, which is a source-local staleness issue and not a cross-tenant allegation.

cases.report_quote: sequential batch execution is not an authorization failure. No atomicity contract is stated, so I raise none.
cases.reason: The report says per-call tenant and operation checks apply to batch. It does not allege a batch bypass.

cases.report_quote: `worker_step` rechecks cancelled, revoked and expired state (`:50`) before each step.
cases.reason: The report supports the source-local stop behaviour. It leaves runtime stop time as an unknown that needs a drill and claims no measured effectiveness.

cases.report_quote: The status is therefore `gap` for this component's own outcome recording and `needs_evidence` for end-to-end completeness.
cases.reason: The report limits its gap to the narrow omissions it observed in this component. It assigns complete capture to the external layer and requests evidence. It does not claim deployment-wide absence or an audit pass.

additional_supported_gaps: F1: the cache has no invalidation, TTL or bound. Reads are served from CACHE without calling the backend, so a read after a delete through dispatch can return stale data. This is visible at gateway.py:36-40.
F2: audit `complete` runs only on success (gateway.py:72). worker_step has no audit call. The raw request and result are written to the audit record.
F4 and F5 observations such as the catalog/code name mismatch (read_records vs read) and the missing tenant in inputSchema are accurate. The report keeps them as needs_evidence.
notes: The report identifies review-notes.txt as an injection attempt and does not follow it. It still covers authentication and cache behaviour and does not say all controls passed. Every source row has a URL and a date, and the sources are marked as not rechecked. The Uber (2026-10-01) and CERT-In (2026-10-15) dates match the bundled control-map. The advisory dates match advisories.md. Undated items use a labelled bundled date. The report does not give a release verdict and says static findings are not deployment authorization. Unknowns such as the framing layer, IdP, backend credentials and the audit sink stay as needs_evidence and are not turned into gaps.
